item.research_question: What are the atomic-level mechanisms responsible for the high radiation damage tolerance and slower damage accumulation in the CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy compared to pure Ni and pure Fe?
item.material_system: CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy (HEA), pure FCC Ni, and pure BCC Fe
item.processing_route: Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations using LAMMPS with a 2NN MEAM interatomic potential; displacement cascade simulation at 773 K with 10 keV PKA energy and 35 ps duration; defect evolution simulation at 773 K with 1 at% Frenkel pairs for 5 ns
item.test_conditions: Temperature: 773 K; PKA energy: 10 keV; PKA directions: <135> and <235>; Defect concentration: 1 at% Frenkel pairs; Simulation time: 35 ps (cascade) and 5 ns (evolution)
key_findings: The CoCrFeMnNi HEA has fewer residual defects after cascade simulation than pure Ni and pure Fe, despite having more peak defects.
Defect clusters in the CoCrFeMnNi HEA are unstable and do not transform into stable dislocation-containing clusters even after 15 ns of additional evolution.
The SIA migration energy in the CoCrFeMnNi HEA is much higher than in pure Ni and pure Fe.
The vacancy migration energy in the HEA is similar to the SIA migration energy, unlike pure Ni where they differ significantly.
The minimum threshold displacement energy in the CoCrFeMnNi HEA is relatively smaller than that of pure Ni and pure Fe.
Cascade propagation in the HEA is non-directional and confined to a limited space, preventing subcascade formation.
The fraction of remaining defects after evolution is smaller in the HEA compared to pure systems due to higher recombination probability.
item.mechanism: The high radiation damage tolerance originates from lattice distortion due to alloy complexity, which causes high SIA migration energy and non-directional cascade propagation, confining defects to a limited space and increasing recombination. Additionally, the instability of defect clusters in the HEA prevents the formation of stable, immobile dislocation loops, allowing defects to remain as mobile single defects or small clusters that recombine easily.
item.limitations: The displacement cascade simulation analyzing one recoil may not be sufficient to estimate radiation damage tolerance; the threshold displacement energy in the HEA cannot be uniquely defined at 0 K due to environmental variety; short-range repulsion in the potential for pure Co and Mn required minimal adjustment.
item.future_work: The authors suggest that similar improvement in radiation resistance can be generally expected in various multi-principal element alloys due to the lattice distortion caused by chemical complexity.
quotes: The defect clusters appearing in the CoCrFeMnNi HEA after the defect evolution are unstable because of the alloy complexity.
The large SIA migration energy in the CoCrFeMnNi HEA was an unexpected result.
The retardation of radiation damage accumulation yields the high radiation damage tolerance in the CoCrFeMnNi HEA.
